title: Linguine alle Vongole
subtitle: Quick seafood pasta in a white wine-style sauce
excerpt: A clam-style quick seafood pasta that delivers clean, bright flavour in under 20 minutes. King prawns stand in for the traditional vongole, making this achievable any night of the week. The sauce is nothing more than garlic, chilli, and a splash of liquid reduced around the seafood.
sourceNotes: Inspired by the classic Neapolitan dish linguine alle vongole, adapted here with prawns as the accessible substitute for fresh clams.

content.text: Fresh clams are the traditional choice for this dish, but king prawns cook in the same time and carry the garlicky sauce just as well. Spaghetti works perfectly here in place of linguine. In place of white wine, a small splash of white wine vinegar mixed with a little water gives the right acidic lift without overpowering the sauce.

items.prepNote: mixed with 50ml water to mimic white wine

content.text: Cook the spaghetti in a large saucepan of well-salted boiling water until just al dente. Reserve a mugful of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over a medium-high heat. Add the garlic and chilli flakes and cook for 1 minute until the garlic is just golden.
Add the prawns and cook for 2 minutes, turning once, until they are just pink.
Pour in the diluted white wine vinegar and let it bubble for 1 minute to cook off the sharp edge.
Add the drained pasta to the pan along with a splash of pasta water. Toss everything together over the heat for 1 minute until the sauce coats the strands.
Remove from the heat, scatter over the parsley, and serve immediately.

items.fix: Pull prawns off the heat as soon as they turn pink.
Let the liquid bubble longer before adding pasta.
Add more reserved pasta water a splash at a time.
